1. The present revision applicant preferred by the State being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of acquittal, passed by the learned 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, Jamnagar, in Criminal Appeal No.22 of 2012, dated 27.11.2012, whereby the appeal of the present respondent - original accused No.1 and 2 came to be allowed and judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 31.03.2012 passed by the learned 5 th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jamnagar, passed in Criminal Case No.3522 of 2004 convicting the respondents - original accused for the breach of State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22130339/
1 Section 7 punishable under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, (for short "
PFA") and sentencing to undergo six months simple imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- in default to undergo one month simple imprisonment, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/02/2026 undefined was set aside.
2.

sentences.text:
The facts of the prosecution, as revealed from the record, in nutshell, are as follows:-
2.1.
That original accused No.1 was the distributor, No.2 was the owner of Santosh Milk House, No.3, is the nominee of the manufacturing firm and No.4 is the firm.
The original complainant - Food Inspector had visited the shop of respondent - original accused No.2 and purchased the sample of Narmada Pasteurinzed Standard Milk.

After doing certain formalities of packing sealing,
drawn the Panchnama and send the sample to the Public Analyst for analysis.

The Public Analyst reported that the sample does not conform to the standards and provisions of the Act and Rules as the percentage of milk fat was less than the prescribed as also mild solid not fat was found less than the prescribed.
After getting sanction, the complainant - Food Inspector has lodged the complaint.

The evidence of complainant was recorded and after the charge was framed and recording of evidence of complainant and Panch witness the having concluded the trial, the learned Magistrate found that accused to have committed breach of Section 2(1-a) as also Section 7 (1) of the PFA which is punishable under Section 16 (1) of the PFA and sentenced original accused No.1 and No.2 to undergo six months simple imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- in default to undergo one month simple imprisonment.
The learned Magistrate acquitted the original accused No.3 and No.4 from the charges leveled against them.

2.2. Against the said judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 31.03.2012 passed by the learned 5 th Additional Chief NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
11/02/2026 undefined Judicial Magistrate, Jamnagar passed in Criminal Case No.3522 of 2004, the respondent herein - the original accused No.1 and 2 had preferred an appeal before the 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, Jamnagar, wherein the learned Session Court has allowed the said appeal and has set aside the judgment and order of trial Court and the respondent -accused have been acquitted from the charges leveled against them.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, the present revision application by the State.

3. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. Rohan Raval would contend that :
3.1. The learned Judge ought to have considered the evidence of complainant - C P Gohil, who has been examined at Exhibit 10.
Witness has deposed in his testimony that he had followed all the necessary procedure prescribed under the law and after obtaining necessary permission from the Court, he had filed a complaint.

The learned Judge ought to have appreciated the evidence of the complainant in true and letter spirit, as the complainant in his evidence before the Court has very categorically stated about the procedure complied with by him while drawing of the sample in the presence of Panch witness and State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22130339/
2 thereafter sending one sample out of three to the Public Analyst and on receipt of the report of Public Analyst, the sanction was obtained to file a case.

entities.text: State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such no lacuna is found in the procedure carried out by the complainant.

3.2. The learned Judge ought to have considered the fact that report of Public Analyst indicates that the sample does not conform to the standards and provisions fo the Act and Rules as the percentage of milk fat was less than the prescribed as also milk solid not fat was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/02/2026 undefined also found less than the prescribed.

3.3. It ought to have been appreciated that there is no reason to disbelieve the report of the Public Analyst because as per the report there is no evidence with regard to tampering with the sample and therefore the benefit of non-examination of the person who conducted the analysis of the sample would not be given to the accused.

3.4. The learned Judge has erroneously come to the conclusion by not believing the report of the Public Analyst which states that sample of the milk does not confirm to the standard of the provisions laid down under the provisions of PFA Rules, 1955.

3.5. The learned Judge has erred in holding that the evidence with regard to the utensils in which the sample was drawn is not dry and clean and thereby procedure laid down under Rule 14 of the Act is violated and benefit of that was given to the respondent-accused.
In fact the learned trial Judge has erroneously come to the conclusion in this regard.

Because the complainant has stated in his evidence with regard to the cleanness of the articles which was used for drawing of the sample and said fact has been supported by Panchnama and therefore it cannot be said that Rule 14 of the Act has been violated for not drawing the sample in clean articles.
3.6. That the offence punishable under the PFA Act are directly connected with the health of the public at large and in the present case there is no reason to disbelieve the evidence of the complainant and contents of the Panchnama because both the evidence are supported from the documentary evidence and therefore also there is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/02/2026 undefined no reason for the Court to disbelieve the evidence of the complainant, and thus, argued to allow the present appeal.
4.
Though served, none appears for the respondents.

5. This Court has gone through the record and proceedings of the case, perused the impugned order dated 31.03.2012, passed by learned 5th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jamnagar, in Criminal Case No. 3522 of 2004 as well as the order dated 27.11.2012, passed by the learned 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, Jamnagar, in Criminal Appeal No.22 of 2012.
6. At the outset, the principle governing the scope of revision are required to be considered.

In the case of Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan v. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke, reported in (2015) 3 SCC 123,
wherein in paragraph 14, it is held that:

3 "14. ...

sentences.text: Unless the order passed by the Magistrate is perverse or the view taken by the court is wholly unreasonable or there is non-consideration of any of relevant material or there is palpable misreading of records, the Revisional Court is not justified in setting aside the order, merely because another view is possible.
The Revisional Court is not meant to act as an appellate court.
The whole purpose of the revisional jurisdiction is to preserve the power in the court to do justice in accordance with the principles of criminal jurisprudence.
The revisional power of the court under Sections 397 to 401 CrPC is not to be equated with that of an appeal.

Unless the finding of the court, whose decision is sought to be revised, is shown to be perverse or untenable in law or is grossly NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
11/02/2026 undefined erroneous or glaringly unreasonable or where the decision is based on no material or where the material facts are wholly ignored or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously, the courts may not interfere with the decision in exercise of their revisional jurisdiction."

6.1. Further, in the case of Southern Sales & Services v. Sauermilch Design and Handels GmbH,
reported in (2008) 14 SCC 457, it is held that "... Revisional Court will not interfere even if a wrong order is passed by a court having jurisdiction, in the absence of a jurisdictional error".

entities.text:
Southern Sales & Services v. Sauermilch Design and Handels GmbH,
reported in (2008) 14 SCC 457
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Thus, from the aforestated principles, it can be said that the High Court can called for and examine the record of any proceedings to satisfy itself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order, however, the revisional power cannot be equated with the power of an appellate court, nor can it be treated as second appellate jurisdiction.

Unless any glaring features is brought to the notice of this Court which otherwise amount to a gross miscarriage of justice,
ordinarily the High Court will not reappreciate the evidence and come to its own conclusion on the same evidence which has been appreciated by the Sessions Judge in appeal.

8. Tested on the aforesaid principle, this Court does not find any palpable error in the face of the record while acquitting the present respondents - original accused by the first appellate court by well reasoned judgment and order, more particularly, pointing out the following discrepancies namely:
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/02/2026 undefined (i) That, the complainant has admitted in his cross- examination that he has not produced on record, the bill of sample purchased from the original accused No.3 and 4.
(ii) That, the measuring cup which was obtained from the shop itself was not washed before drawing sample.
(iii) The cup for drawing samples was handedover to the accused person after taking the sample.

State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22130339/
4 (iv) That he has not verified whether the cup used for drawing sample was clean or not.

entities.text: State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (v) As per the prescribed procedure, after drawing sample formalin which required to be added to the milk and after properly mixing has to be packed in three sample bottles, however, in case on hand the sample was collected in three separate bottles and in each bottle 20 drops of formalin were added which is not the proper method for mixing formalin as prescribed under law.

(vi) That, the original accused No.3 and 4 are the persons who have manufacture and packed the milk in question who have been acquitted, however, present respondents - original accused No.1 and 2 have came to be convicted who were only selling the packed milk manufactured by original accused No.3 and 4.
(vii) That, the Pancha's have turned hostile and not supported the case of the prosecution.

NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/518/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/02/2026 undefined (viii) That, the prosecution has failed to prove that formalin which came to be added in the sample of the milk were in accordance with the quantity as prescribed under the relevant rules.
(ix) That, the mandatory provision of Section 11 read with Rule 16 was also not followed in its true and letter spirit.
(x) That, except the complainant, no other witness has supported the case of the the prosecution.

9. In view of the aforestated factual aspects, the first appellate court does not find that the mandatory provision of law of drawing sample, mixing of formalin, quantity of formalin in accordance with the relevant rules, etc. were in accordance with law which demolishes the case of the prosecution, this Court does not find that the appellate court has committed any patent defect or error of jurisdictional or law which requires to be set aside.

Thus, this Court does not dwell at the length upon the fact and evidence of the case to reverse those finding, more particularly, when the reasoned judgment and order of acquittal is passed by the first appellate court, and no glaring feature is brought to the notice of this Court which can amounts to gross miscarriage of justice.
10. Under the circumstance, the present revision application stands dismissed.
Rule is discharged.

(P. M. RAVAL, J) NITIN MAKWANA State Of Gujarat vs Jethalal Pritamdas Khetani on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22130339/
